name: Global temperature
summary: Global temperature 2.14°C above pre-industrial on 21 Nov, a record for the date and above the 1.6°C Alert line
state: ERA5 data for 21 Nov put global surface air temperature about 2.14°C above pre-industrial levels (14.45°C absolute), a record high for the calendar date and well above the 1.6°C Alert line (Climate Reanalyzer). The estimate adds 0.88°C to the 1991–2020 anomaly of about 1.26°C, up from 2.09°C on 20 Nov. Readings have stayed above 1.6°C through November as the very strong El Niño adds heat.
for_you: Record global heat raises the odds of extreme weather, including heatwaves in the southern-hemisphere summer and heavy rainfall; follow national met service warnings where you live or travel.
rubric_hit: +2.14°C > +1.6°C Alert line; record for the date
why: Global temperature is the master climate variable; each tenth of a degree raises extreme-weather risk.
drivers: Greenhouse gases, El Niño/La Niña, aerosols, solar cycle.

rubric.alert: > +1.6°C, or a record high for the calendar date.
rubric.normal: Daily global anomaly < +1.3°C above pre-industrial (ERA5 vs 1991–2020 + 0.88°C).
